rules.text: Never block the JavaFX application thread. No file or network I/O, no process start or wait, no parsing, searching, hashing or JSON of any size on it, and no `Thread.sleep`, `Future.get()`, `join()` or `Process.waitFor()` there.

rules.text: Blocking work stays off the common `ForkJoinPool`, and a `Process` subclass overrides `onExit()`.

rules.text: Every row of every menu the app draws carries an icon that depicts it. A command row wears its command's glyph; a row that names a thing rather than an action (a recent file, a branch, a project) wears that thing's icon; a submenu wears its family's. Only a check or radio row goes without, because its mark fills the icon column. Where the icon set has no glyph that depicts a command, the app adds one (a Material 24 dp path, or a line glyph in the kit's style) instead of leaving the row blank or borrowing another command's.
rules.why: a menu is scanned before it is read, and the glyph is what the eye finds first; the same glyph on the toolbar, in the palette and in the menu ([ICON-20](https://pauta-project.dev/4.0.1/icons-and-color/#icon-20)) is learned once. A blank cell breaks the column, and a borrowed glyph says something else.
